facts.claim: 作者把整章编成食物笑话集，从正餐、零食到饮料都要挨一句双关，如冰淇淋厂那条
facts.quote: I got sacked from my job at the ice cream factory for refusing to work on sundaes.

facts.claim: 作者用 spill the beans（说漏嘴／撒豆子）开场，让亨氏工厂被解雇的原因始终悬着
facts.quote: ‘I’m not going to tell you what I did to get sacked from the Heinz factory.’ ‘Spill the beans?’ ‘I’ve already said, I’m not going to tell you.’

facts.claim: 作者把宗教套话叠到热狗点单上：make me one with everything 既是‘全料’也是‘与万物合一’
facts.quote: What did the Buddhist say to the hot dog seller? ‘Make me one with everything.’

facts.claim: 作者在食物笑话之后另开奶酪小节，用 debris／de camembert 的谐音作该节开场
facts.quote: ‘Debris everywhere?’ ‘Yes, and de camembert’s scattered around too.’

facts.claim: 作者反复用「What do you call…?」造词式问句（impasta 即 impostor／pasta）
facts.quote: What do you call a fake noodle? An impasta.

facts.claim: 作者用两件食物对话的形式，让‘会说话’本身取代谐音成为反转
facts.quote: Two sausages are sizzling in a pan. One says, ‘Wow, it’s hot in here!’ The other says, ‘WHOA! A TALKING SAUSAGE!’

facts.claim: 作者把沙漠不缺食物解释成‘到处都是三明治’，靠 sandwich 的字面‘沙’义
facts.quote: Why do people never go hungry in the desert? Because of all the sandwiches there.

facts.claim: 作者以奶酪小节收尾，用 shooting the breeze／cheddar 双关结束全章
facts.quote: ‘Shooting the breeze?’ ‘Yes, and firing arrows at the cheddar.’

relations.relation: 作者把双关藏在答句里，读者须自己完成谐音还原（chew-chew／choo-choo）
relations.quote: What do you call a train filled with bubblegum? A chew-chew train.

relations.relation: 朋友提出‘苹果是黄色且弯的’这一荒谬前提，叙述者用水果名回敬其荒唐
relations.quote: My friend told me apples are yellow and bendy. I said, ‘That’s bananas!’

relations.pair: 一只盘子 / 另一只盘子
relations.relation: 一只盘子用 on me 请客，既指‘我付账’也指‘菜在我身上’
relations.quote: What did one plate say to the other? ‘Dinner is on me!’

numbers.meaning: 四驱车被说成能碾过 pâté 状物，靠 all-terrine／all-terrain 谐音
numbers.quote: I’ve got a four-wheel-drive car that can easily cross coarse, pâté-like substances. It’s an all-terrine vehicle.

numbers.meaning: 比咬到整条虫更糟的是咬到半条，答案把‘更糟’落到剩余部分
numbers.quote: What’s worse than biting into an apple and finding a worm? Biting into an apple and finding half a worm.

numbers.meaning: 作者称人吃的香蕉比猴子多，因为大多数人连一只猴子都没吃过
numbers.quote: It sounds unbelievable, but people eat more bananas than monkeys. It’s true, most people never even eat one monkey.
